title: Data Centers and Communities
summary: Communities can study both the opportunities and the questions that come with infrastructure.
objectives: Identify possible benefits of data-center development.
Ask balanced questions about energy, water, land, taxes, sustainability, and community benefits.

vocab.def: A positive result or investment that helps people in a community.
Planning to meet needs while caring for resources and future communities.

sections.heading: Possible opportunities
sections.body: A data center may bring construction activity, infrastructure investment, local business activity, and jobs. These outcomes depend on real plans and should be checked with evidence.

sections.heading: Important questions
sections.body: People may ask about electricity, water, land, noise, taxes, sustainability, roads, and who benefits. Asking a question is not the same as reaching a conclusion.

sections.heading: Listen to more than one view
sections.body: Residents, schools, developers, utilities, workers, and environmental groups may notice different effects. Good community learning makes room for evidence and respectful questions.

practice.prompt: Create two columns: one possible opportunity and one question a community should investigate.

quiz.question: What is a balanced way to study a new data center?
options: Examine possible benefits and community questions
quiz.answer: Examine possible benefits and community questions

reflectionPrompt: What would you want to know if a data center were planned near your community?
